newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in, buys dollars - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in, buys dollars - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Korea stepped into the interbank market shortly before trading closed on Monday, buying dollars to cap the local currency's rise, dealers said.
They said the bank bought dollars at 888.00 won, immediately pulling down the local currency to 888.90 won per dollar.
Bank of Korea officials were not immediately available for comment.
Dealers said the local currency had been under upward pressure in line with the Japanese yen's recent strength against the greenback in international markets.
The won was trading as high as 887.80 against the dollar won when the central bank stepped in.
